cohort: Women who delivered vaginally at Peking University Third Hospital between January 1, 2014, and June 30, 2018, and were followed up 1 year postpartum.
finding: Infant birth weight of 3,400 g or more, forceps-assisted vaginal delivery, midline episiotomy, and second to fourth-degree perineal tear were identified as independent risk factors for anal incontinence during the first year following vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Forceps-assisted vaginal delivery, midline episiotomy, and second to fourth-degree perineal tear were found to increase the risk of postpartum anal incontinence after vaginal delivery.
